Silver (Biblical)
SIL-ver
noun
Hebrew keseph (H3701), Greek argyrion (G694) — the precious metal, in Scripture pervasively associated with the price of redemption, the atonement money, and the betrayal of Christ for thirty pieces (Matt 26:15; Zech 11:12-13). The second-most-mentioned metal in the Bible after gold.

See also: Silver (Biblical)

📖 Biblical Definition

Silver in biblical theology is the metal of THE PRICE OF REDEMPTION. The atonement money for the soul of every Israelite was half a shekel of silver (Exod 30:13-16) — "the rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel" — equal in soul-price before God. The firstborn of Israel were redeemed with five shekels of silver each (Num 18:16). The kinsman-redeemer paid silver to purchase back forfeited inheritance (Ruth 4 — Boaz; the price is given in silver). And Christ Himself was sold for thirty pieces of silver (Matt 26:14-16) — the price of a slave under Exodus 21:32 — fulfilling the prophecy of Zechariah 11:12-13 to the dollar. "The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times" (Ps 12:6) — silver is the metal of the refined and tested word; "the tongue of the just is as choice silver" (Prov 10:20). Solomon's silver was so abundant in his reign that it was reckoned of no value (1 Kings 10:21) — but the silver that mattered most was the silver of redemption. The thirty pieces of silver thrown back into the temple by Judas (Matt 27:5) — and used to buy the potter's field for burial of strangers (Matt 27:7) — created a graveyard out of the price of Christ. Silver is the metal of REDEMPTION-PAID. Wherever silver appears in Scripture, the question is: redemption of what? for whom? by what price? Christ Himself was the silver-redeemed slave, and at His resurrection the silver became the down-payment of an inheritance unfading.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The precious white metal of redemption-price; the atonement half-shekel, the kinsman-redeemer's payment, the thirty pieces of Christ's betrayal.

expand to see more

SILVER, noun. A white precious metal, second only to gold in the biblical economy. Used for currency, ornament, sacred vessels, and the price of redemption.

In Scripture, the atonement half-shekel for every Israelite soul (Exod 30:13-16); the redemption price for the firstborn (Num 18:16); the betrayal price of Christ (Matt 26:15; fulfilling Zech 11:12-13); the refined-word metaphor (Ps 12:6); the kinsman-redeemer's purchase price (Ruth 4).

📖 Key Scripture

Matthew 26:15 — "And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver."

Exodus 30:13 — "This they shall give, every one that passeth among them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary: (a shekel is twenty gerahs:) an half shekel shall be the offering of the LORD."

Psalm 12:6 — "The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times."

Zechariah 11:12-13 — "And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Silver is corrupted when its consistent biblical theme of redemption-price is reduced to mere currency (treating the half-shekel as ancient tax, the thirty pieces as random sum) or when modern translations replace "silver" with "money" in contexts where the metal's specific theological weight matters.

expand to see more

Currency-flattening. Modern translations often replace "silver" with "money" or "coins" for readability, but in doing so they lose the canonical chain. "Thirty pieces of silver" is not just "some money" — it is the EXACT price of a slave under Exodus 21:32, fulfilling Zechariah 11:12-13 down to the shekel. "Half a shekel" of silver is not just "a tax" — it is the atonement money for the soul of every Israelite, equal for rich and poor. The metal carries theological weight that mere currency loses.

Atonement-money severance. The temple half-shekel (Exod 30:13-16) was a yearly reminder that EVERY soul required a redemption price — the rich could not pay more, the poor could not pay less. Modernist commentary often treats this as ancient temple economics, missing the gospel logic: every soul has the same value to God, and every soul requires the same atonement. Christ's silver-redemption of His people is the same gospel: a price that does not vary by the soul's wealth, paid by another for those who could not pay.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew keseph (H3701), Greek argyrion (G694) — silver; the metal of the price of redemption in biblical theology.

expand to see more

Hebrew keseph (H3701) — silver; root meaning "to long for, desire" — the metal of what people desire / pay for

Greek argyrion (G694) — silver, silver coin; the thirty pieces of Christ's betrayal (Matt 26:15)

Atonement half-shekel for every Israelite soul (Exod 30:13-16) — the equality-of-soul-price theology

Price of a slave (Exod 21:32) = thirty shekels = Zechariah's prophesied price = Christ's actual betrayal price

Usage

"Christ was sold for thirty pieces of silver — the exact price of a slave, the prophet's stated price, the gospel's redemption price."

"Every Israelite paid half a shekel of silver for his soul — the rich no more, the poor no less; the gospel knows no two-tier atonement."

"Silver is the metal of redemption-paid: every appearance in Scripture asks the question, redemption of what, for whom, by what price?"
